evidence.title: BMW: humanoid pilot and Leipzig programme
evidence.observation_period: 2025 Spartanburg pilot; December 2025 Leipzig test; future 2026 pilot
evidence.claim: Figure 02 moved more than 90,000 components over around 1,250 operating hours and supported over 30,000 X3 vehicles; BMW selected a highly automated body shop with integration expertise. AEON underwent a Leipzig test in December 2025.
evidence.locator: Sections 'Successful pilot at BMW Group Plant Spartanburg' and 'First pilot project with humanoid robots in Europe'
evidence.verification: Primary text retrieved with Exa web_fetch and inspected; no independent field replication.
evidence.limitations: No shift-by-shift autonomy, intervention, downtime, staffing, cost or robot-count denominator. Future summer 2026 AEON pilot status is not verified by this February release.

evidence.title: F.02 contributed to production of 30,000 cars
evidence.observation_period: 11-month deployment; six months daily runtime as stated
evidence.claim: Figure reports 90,000+ loaded parts and 1,250+ operational hours; 84-second total cycle/37-second loading were requirements, >99% placement was a target and zero interventions per shift was a goal. Forearm failures informed Figure 03 wrist redesign; Figure 02 returned to HQ for retirement.
evidence.locator: 'Deployment Overview'; 'Hardware Reliability and Learnings'
evidence.verification: Primary text retrieved with Exa web_fetch and inspected; no independent field replication.
evidence.limitations: Targets are not realized measurements. 'Minimal hardware failures' has no count or exposure-adjusted rate. 10-hour shifts and deployment months do not imply continuous operation for every elapsed hour.
evidence.conflict_note: Figure describes 11-month deployment; BMW describes support within ten months. Preserve different calendar boundaries; do not average.

evidence.title: BMW Figure 03 sequencing project
evidence.claim: Figure 03 logistics sequence is components from unsorted containers to a sequencing trolley, then tugger train or STR transport to assembly employees. BMW also uses virtual factory tools for manual ergonomics and AIQX quality inspection.
evidence.locator: 'Next step with the next-generation Figure 03 robot'; 'BMW iFACTORY applications'
evidence.verification: Primary text retrieved with Exa web_fetch and inspected; no independent field replication.
evidence.limitations: Prospective workflow, not a measured sustained production result. Do not inherit Figure 02 throughput/reliability or attribute BMW digital gains to humanoids.

evidence.title: GXO multi-year Agility RaaS agreement
evidence.observation_period: Late 2023 proof of concept; June 2024 commercial deployment
evidence.claim: GXO deployed Digit and Agility Arc under a multi-year RaaS agreement at a SPANX facility; Digit moves totes from AMRs/cobots onto conveyors.
evidence.locator: Opening paragraphs and descriptions of Agility Arc/SPANX
evidence.verification: Primary text retrieved with Exa web_fetch and inspected; no independent field replication.
evidence.limitations: No installed robot count, unit price, staffing, intervention, elapsed operating hours or ROI calculation.

evidence.title: Digit moves over 100,000 totes
evidence.claim: Digit moved over 100,000 totes at GXO Flowery Branch; manufacturer describes AMR-to-conveyor and floor stacking and a pipeline blending traditional control, teleoperated demonstrations, RL and simulation.
evidence.locator: Opening milestone; 'Deploying Humanoids'; 'Translating AI Hype'
evidence.verification: Primary text retrieved with Exa web_fetch and inspected; no independent field replication.
evidence.limitations: Cumulative cycles do not give per-robot throughput, accepted output quality, assistance burden or positive ROI. Customer confirms commercial arrangement in CAP-E004, not this cumulative metric.

evidence.title: Mercedes Digital Factory Campus: Apollo and MO360
evidence.claim: Apollo collects production-environment data; employees transfer knowledge through teleoperation and augmented reality; autonomous operations are described as the next step. MO360 chatbots and virtual agents also support human production staff.
evidence.locator: Apollo paragraphs; 'Artificial intelligence for everyone'
evidence.verification: Primary text retrieved with Exa web_fetch and inspected; no independent field replication.
evidence.limitations: Testing/data collection cannot be classified as autonomous labor replacement. No causal productivity estimate or deployed exposure.

evidence.title: Atlas Robotics Metaplant Application Center opens
evidence.claim: RMAC is operational as a testbed/training center; Atlas is training on automotive logistics/sequencing. Future expansion, 25,000 group units and 30,000-unit annual production facility are plans.
evidence.locator: Opening; RMAC operations; 'About Boston Dynamics'
evidence.verification: Primary text retrieved with Exa web_fetch and inspected; no independent field replication.
evidence.limitations: Training-center operation is not commercial production throughput. Article calls Atlas 'currently in development'; no trial success, intervention or productive fleet size.

evidence.title: Data Scaling Laws in Imitation Learning for Robotic Manipulation
evidence.observation_period: Controlled manipulation experiments; initial submission 2024; inspected v3
evidence.claim: More than 40,000 demonstrations and 15,000 rollouts support diversity-dependent improvement on four tasks. Fits use six data points, with 1–32 objects/environments; repeated demonstrations saturate and action-network size did not improve monotonically.
evidence.locator: Sections 3–7; Fig.5; Table1; Table2; footnote1 in §4.2
evidence.verification: Primary text retrieved with Exa web_fetch and inspected; no independent field replication. Submission history directly retrieved and inspected on2026-10-25; exact version date verified.
evidence.limitations: Publication date denotes initial submission; inspected v3 dated2025-10-13. Fits concern normalized partial-credit score gap, not commercial success/output. Only two tasks drive detailed fit; two more test collection recipe; no task-level generalization or universal exponent. Newer v4 exists; only specified core sections compared, not a complete semantic diff.

newer_version_check.result: Checked core results unchanged: six-point normalized-score-gap fits;1191-pair extrapolation remains unverified; Table1 success85.0/92.5/87.5/90.0percent; Table2 small/base/large U-Net scores0.88/0.90/0.83. Preserve v3 snapshot; no full-version semantic comparison or experiment replication.

evidence.title: Open X-Embodiment: datasets and RT-X
evidence.claim: Repository spans 22 embodiments, but experiments train on nine manipulator embodiments; 3,600 evaluations across six robots. RT-1-X improves mean success on small-data tasks, but Google-robot setting gives 73% versus RT-1 92%. RT-2-X emergent-skills scores 75.8% versus RT-2 27.3%.
evidence.locator: §IV-C; Table I; §V; Table II; §VI
evidence.verification: Primary text retrieved with Exa web_fetch and inspected; no independent field replication. Submission history directly retrieved and inspected on2026-10-25; exact version date verified.
evidence.limitations: Known embodiments and coarsely aligned 7D end-effector actions; not generalization to new robots or radically different modalities. Table I does not support blanket claim larger model beats every baseline (91% vs 92% on Google setting). No production economics.
evidence.source_internal_conflict: Narrative 'outperforms' in large-data discussion is broader than Table I; retain the table values.

evidence.title: DataMIL: selecting data with datamodels
evidence.claim: DataMIL selects training samples using target-policy influence; target validation loss, temporal clustering and target co-training are central. It evaluates more than 60 simulation/real tasks and four real-world OXE target tasks including new Tiago embodiment.
evidence.locator: 'Proxy Metric'; 'Co-Training with Target'; 'OXE Results'; 'What data does DataMIL select?'
evidence.verification: Primary text retrieved with Exa web_fetch and inspected; no independent field replication.
evidence.limitations: Selection needs target data and computation. Visually similar observations can have helpful or harmful action distributions; no demonstrated market-wide transferable dataset value.

evidence.title: pi0.5 open-world generalization
evidence.claim: pi0.5 combines heterogeneous knowledge sources and controls mobile manipulators in unseen homes; paper evaluates three homes and stage-completion rubrics. Authors acknowledge semantic and motor mistakes.
evidence.locator: Blog 'Generalization to new homes' and 'Where do we go from here?'; paper §V and Fig.7
evidence.verification: Primary text retrieved with Exa web_fetch and inspected; no independent field replication.
evidence.limitations: New-home generalization is not a representative household service audit; tasks and quality rubrics remain bounded. Human feedback, resets, sample sizes and economic outcomes require granular review.

evidence.title: pi*0.6: a VLA that learns from experience
evidence.claim: RECAP uses demonstrations, on-policy experience and expert corrections. On-robot training more than doubles throughput for the diverse-laundry experiment evaluated on button-up shirts and for espresso. Diverse-laundry training covers11 item types; simple laundry iterations use300 trajectories on four robots per iteration. SectionVI-C describes box iterations as600 autonomous trials and360 intervention trials; AppendixA-F calls the600 demonstrations.
evidence.locator: SectionVI-A Laundry(diverse items); SectionsVI-B/C; Figures7–12; SectionVII; AppendixA-F Dataset composition
evidence.verification: Primary text retrieved with Exa web_fetch and inspected; no independent field replication. Submission history directly retrieved and inspected on2026-10-25; exact version date verified.
evidence.limitations: Initial submission2025-11-18; inspected v2 dated2025-11-19. Diverse-laundry quantitative evaluation covers button-up shirts only, not the full11-type training mixture. Success uses task-specific deadlines and human quality annotation. Figure9 box-throughput point estimate first declines then improves; overlapping early error bars do not establish a statistically significant decline. Research results do not establish typical24/7 deployment economics. SectionVII retains human reward labeling, interventions and episode resets; updates are batch/offline. Inconsistent box-data terminology prevents inferring that all600 trials are unassisted or equating them with a measured labor cost.
evidence.source_internal_conflict: SectionVI-C calls600 box episodes per iteration autonomous trials; AppendixA-F Dataset composition calls them demonstrations. Both give360 correction/intervention episodes; collection assistance cannot be resolved from terminology alone.
evidence.training_population: Diverse laundry trained on11 item types; simple laundry and other task-specific mixtures separately described.
evidence.evaluation_population: Diverse-laundry quantitative experiment: button-up shirts only. Separate simple/targeted laundry, double espresso and box-assembly evaluations.

evidence.title: F.02 Decommission
evidence.observation_period: Fleet-status statement as of September 30, 2026; individual retirement dates and unit counts undisclosed
evidence.geography: Figure fleet; headquarters and described disposal activity, not a matched BMW operating cohort
evidence.claim: Figure reports most of its Figure 02 fleet has been decommissioned, with a few units stored at headquarters. It describes maintaining the older generation as unattractive while the successor fleet grows and disassembly as competing for technical staff time.
evidence.locator: Opening fleet-maintenance rationale and final fleet-status paragraph
evidence.verification: Primary dated manufacturer article retrieved and inspected; no independent asset inventory or recovery valuation.
evidence.limitations: No exact retired/retained count, disposal dates, contract treatment, salvage value or customer asset life. Does not date a new BMW shutdown or measure Figure 03 output; no stunt performance is used as production evidence.

evidence.title: Random bin picking for feeding car body parts
evidence.observation_period: Dingolfing line entrance reported operating since 2020; article in 2022 edition
evidence.geography: Dingolfing, Germany; not the Spartanburg humanoid station
evidence.locator: Evotion 2022 breadcrumb; Complete package; Design challenges; Automated parts feeding; Installation in record time
evidence.claim: Describes BMW body-panel feeding with vision, suction gripping, double-part detection and an intermediate buffer. The cell integrates logistics calls and plant controls; upstream feasibility, preassembly and testing preceded onsite commissioning.
evidence.limitations: Different site, parts and process from Figure. No matched cost, staffing, intervention or acceptance denominator; no verified 2026 retention. The reported single-component process time cannot be ranked against a three-part loading requirement.

quantities.denominator: One component; buffered feeder process, not a three-part fixture set or observed timing distribution
Onsite phase after advance feasibility, complete preassembly and extensive tests; not total project lead time
quantities.period: Installation associated with line operating since 2020

evidence.title: F.03 Arrives at BMW
evidence.observation_period: First Figure 03 logistics demonstration at BMW; exposure duration undisclosed
evidence.locator: Highlights; Sequencing Use Case; Bringing Helix to Life on the Factory Floor
evidence.claim: Figure 03 with Helix 02 demonstrates variable-pose part sequencing and cart pulling. Figure claims the combined manipulation/mobility workflow is infeasible for traditional fixed automation.
evidence.limitations: No sustained accepted-output, intervention or cost denominator. A claimed limit of fixed hard-coded motions does not establish a limit of vision-guided fixed cells, separate transport or redesigned presentation. CAP-E025 is a different-workflow comparator, not a matched refutation of cart manipulation.

evidence.title: Leipzig debut: BMW Group introduces humanoid robots – a first in Germany

evidence.limitations: Past and prospective schedule wording coexist; no achieved pilot duration, sustained Figure 03 result or net staffing effect. Repeated Figure 02 totals are the earlier evidence lineage, not independent corroboration.

learning_relationships.source_system: UMI demonstrations; Diffusion Policy with DINOv2 visual encoder
learning_relationships.output: normalized score gap and task success on unseen objects/environments
learning_relationships.fit_domain: 1–32 objects/environments; six fit points; two primary tasks; two additional collection-recipe tasks
learning_relationships.findings: Repeated demonstrations saturate; 32 pairs×50 demos proposed for similar task difficulty; action U-Net scaling does not improve monotonically.
learning_relationships.uncertainty: Four tasks; tester partial-credit rubric; no new-task transfer; 1191-pair extrapolation left untested by authors.
learning_relationships.permitted_model_use: Data-diversity/selection mechanism and sensitivity bounds; no general productivity coefficient.
learning_relationships.missing_reason: No supported universal humanoid scaling law.

learning_relationships.source_system: RT1-X and RT2-X; nine training manipulators
learning_relationships.fit_domain: 3600 trials across six robots; known modalities/embodiments
learning_relationships.findings: Positive transfer in small-data settings; RT1-X negative comparison on Google robot 73% vs92%; RT2-X emergent75.8% vs27.3% baseline, generalization61% vs62%.
learning_relationships.uncertainty: Different task distributions; not a power-law fit; no unseen-embodiment proof.
learning_relationships.permitted_model_use: Directed, conditional transfer edges; negative/neutral transfer scenarios.

learning_relationships.source_system: Target-policy data influence and OXE prior
learning_relationships.fit_domain: >60 simulation/real tasks; four real-world target tasks
learning_relationships.findings: Task-aware selection can outperform semantic similarity; visually similar actions can help or harm.
learning_relationships.uncertainty: Target data and proxy validation required; no generic dollar value per robot-hour.
learning_relationships.permitted_model_use: Price collection/selection/evaluation separately; transfer value conditional on rights and validation.

learning_relationships.fit_domain: Three unseen homes in paper; bounded household tasks
learning_relationships.findings: New-environment transfer demonstrated; model still makes semantic/motor mistakes.
learning_relationships.uncertainty: No representative household time-use sample, full-service success or labor saving estimate.
learning_relationships.permitted_model_use: Qualitative prior for adaptation costs; not calibrated household penetration.

learning_relationships.output: successful tasks per hour and success within task deadline
learning_relationships.fit_domain: Simple/targeted laundry; diverse-laundry quantitative evaluation restricted to button-up shirts despite11-type training; espresso double-shot; box assembly; two iterative updates studied
learning_relationships.findings: More than doubled throughput for the button-up-shirt diverse-laundry evaluation and espresso; box-throughput point estimate initially decreases before later gain, with overlapping early error bars. Simple-laundry iterations omit expert corrections while box iterations include them; human labels/resets remain.
learning_relationships.uncertainty: Task deadlines200/500/600s; human quality labels; no representative field operating-cost denominator. Human reward labels, interventions and resets remain; batched offline updates. SectionVI-C calls600 box episodes autonomous trials, AppendixA-F calls them demonstrations; do not infer fully unassisted collection or a statistically significant early throughput decline.
learning_relationships.permitted_model_use: Learning can affect throughput and recovery; preserve training costs/delays and nonmonotonic scenario.

learning_relationships.fit_domain: Forearm failure point at single deployment
learning_relationships.findings: Field exposure informs removal of wrist distribution board/dynamic cabling.
learning_relationships.uncertainty: Improvement magnitude unreported; retrofit not established.
learning_relationships.permitted_model_use: New-generation benefit only until compatible retrofit proven.

market_implications.useful_output: Accepted components loaded/sequenced at required takt and quality
market_implications.human_baseline: Human loading/kitting with existing automated transport, fixtures and digital quality tools
market_implications.digital_only: Planning/ergonomics/quality exception aids; measured labor effect unknown
market_implications.specialized_alternative: Qualified vision-guided fixed cell with gripper, buffer and replenishment; explicit presentation redesign and separate transport are additional alternatives.
market_implications.mixed_configuration: Humanoid bridges variable human-designed manipulation; fixed robots weld; STRs transport
market_implications.conditional_unlock: Sustained takt, measured intervention/recovery, hardware durability and integration cost
market_implications.conclusion: A bounded humanoid station must earn its incremental handling/mobility value against qualified conventional vision and process redesign; actual matched economics remain unknown.

market_implications.useful_output: Accepted standardized tote transferred to downstream flow
market_implications.digital_only: WMS/dispatch/arrival scheduling; effect must be measured separately
market_implications.specialized_alternative: Docking/lift/conveyor modification or fixed/mobile transfer arm
market_implications.mixed_configuration: Digit plus existing AMR/conveyor, human exception support
market_implications.conditional_unlock: Peak-hour throughput, supervisor queue, charge/downtime, safety and all-in cost
market_implications.conclusion: Commercial revenue is established by operator announcement; comparative ROI and labor replacement are not. Stretch carton-unloading rates cannot be assigned to tote transfer.

market_implications.useful_output: Area cleaned to specified cleanliness plus explicit separate clutter-removal services
market_implications.human_baseline: Cleaner using powered equipment and digital scheduling
market_implications.digital_only: Routing/work orders/inventory scheduling improve existing crews
market_implications.mixed_configuration: Specialized cleaner plus human clutter/exceptions; manipulator only when added service validated
market_implications.conditional_unlock: Clutter handling, chemicals/wet-floor safety, accepted cleanliness, service staffing
market_implications.conclusion: Home manipulation research does not establish full commercial cleaning; divide complementary output rather than assign total floor-cleaning hours to humanoids.

market_implications.useful_output: Correct item delivered with chain-of-custody and service deadline
market_implications.digital_only: Queue prioritization and scheduling; no uplift calibrated
market_implications.specialized_alternative: Wheeled hospital delivery AMR with lift/door integration
market_implications.mixed_configuration: AMR transport plus human loading/handover; manipulator only at validated boundaries
market_implications.conditional_unlock: Infrastructure permissions, infection control, routing around people, exception recovery
market_implications.conclusion: Institutional integration and shared elevators may bind before bipedal mobility; clinical care capability is outside this evidence.

market_implications.useful_output: Installed element accepted under trade/site quality requirements
market_implications.human_baseline: Tradespeople with digital plans, lifts and power tools
market_implications.mixed_configuration: Human-supervised specialty robot and human finishing
market_implications.conditional_unlock: Weather/terrain, forceful manipulation, task variation, tool changes and recovery
market_implications.conclusion: Inspected tabletop and structured-factory transfer evidence cannot calibrate construction installation eligibility.

market_implications.useful_output: Actionable inspected condition leading to maintenance decision; repair separate
market_implications.conditional_unlock: Access, inspection data quality, downstream action, and intervention resources
market_implications.conclusion: Humanoid dexterity matters only for proven interaction/repair needs; sensor missions are not repair output. Field dossiers owned by I/J.

questions.decision_consequence: Changes viability and support-limited fleet scale in current entry cells.
questions.question: What are measured intervention arrivals, duration, queue bursts and accepted throughput for Digit and Figure across full shifts?
questions.evidence_target: Operator logs with robot count, scheduled/active time, failed attempts, resets, quality and retained staffing.
questions.stopping_condition: Compatible multi-shift denominator and full support allocation or explicit field-access block.
questions.next_action: Search operator technical presentations and safety/operations disclosures; field access requires separate authority.

questions.decision_consequence: Determines whether deployment generates transferable learning or mostly repetitive production.
questions.question: Which source deployments improve target performance after controlling diversity, policy version, compute and target data?
questions.evidence_target: Held-out task/site/embodiment ablations including negative transfer, total costs and rights.
questions.stopping_condition: At least one target-specific learning edge validated with cost/delay; otherwise scenario only.
questions.next_action: Extract full DataMIL and contemporary VLA target comparisons; preserve no-transfer baseline.

questions.decision_consequence: Separates software upgrades from new-generation capex and downtime.
questions.question: Which improvements can existing fleets actually adopt?
questions.evidence_target: Hardware/software compatibility and warranty/validation requirements; retrofit cost and downtime.
questions.stopping_condition: Version-specific supported upgrade matrix for one commercial fleet.
questions.next_action: Trace Figure02 retirement/Figure03 and Digit platform support disclosures.

questions.decision_consequence: Tests economic value of biped versus cheaper/more reliable specialization.
questions.question: At matched useful output, does humanoid flexibility offset support and integration costs against fixed/wheeled alternatives?
questions.evidence_target: Matched output, quality, staffing, redesign/maintenance costs, demand mix and operating exposure.
questions.stopping_condition: At least one source-supported comparative estimate or threshold-only model with missing inputs.
questions.next_action: Deepen automotive fixture loading and 3PL tote bridge alternatives with atlas/FG/I teams.

questions.decision_consequence: Determines whether coordinated scale adds throughput or congestion.
questions.question: Which coordination decisions and infrastructure permissions measurably improve a heterogeneous site?
questions.evidence_target: Control/state/API boundaries, common resource utilization, fallback, latency and before/after service outcomes.
questions.stopping_condition: One causal or carefully matched operational comparison; otherwise mechanism-only.
questions.next_action: Join Open-RMF/Arc interface records to hospital and 3PL operator observations.

questions.question: What current operator-supported results exist for AEON, Apollo, Walker, Sanctuary, NEURA/Fourier and Asian providers beyond the inspected announcements?
questions.evidence_target: Dated operator/certification/technical data rather than orders and edited demonstrations.
questions.stopping_condition: Regional/provider coverage register with explicit negative or unavailable evidence.
questions.next_action: Target Chinese-language operator reports and current 2026 technical disclosures.

workcell_comparison.shared_service: Correct component set at specified fixture/sequence handoff by its deadline, with accepted identity, pose and quality. Downstream welding, transport and whole vehicles are distinct.
workcell_comparison.comparison_warning: The installed single-component buffered feeder, Figure 02 three-part loading requirements and Figure 03 sequencing/cart demonstration are not a shared measured denominator.
workcell_comparison.strong_conventional_comparator: Vision-guided fixed cell with explicit staging buffer, part-specific gripping, double-part checks and material replenishment, plus prepared presentation where its upstream work is counted.
